ko_meaning_en: A country in East Asia

example.en: I want to go to Korea.

tokens.note: 에 marks the place you go to

form.q_en: Pick the particle for the place you want to go.
form.why: 에 marks the place you go to. 이 marks a subject, 의 means 'of', and 와 is only used after a vowel.

ko_meaning_en: A place like Korea or the United States

tokens.note: 가 marks the subject after a vowel
크다 drops ㅡ: 크 + 어요 → 커요

form.q_en: Pick the particle that makes 'country' the subject.
form.why: 가 marks the subject after a vowel; 이 is used after a consonant. 를 marks an object and 에 means 'at/to'.

ko_meaning_en: A country that is not your own

tokens.note: 이 marks the subject after a consonant
에서 marks where an action happens

form.q_en: Pick the particle for the place where he works.
form.why: 에서 marks the place where an action (working) happens. 에 is for where something is or where you go.

ko_meaning_en: The language used in the US and the UK

tokens.note: 는 marks the topic after a vowel
를 marks the object after a vowel

form.q_en: Pick the particle that makes 'English' the object.
form.why: 를 marks the object after a vowel; 을 is used after a consonant. 에 and 가 do not mark an object.

ko_meaning_en: Sounds or talk that people make with their mouth

tokens.note: 을 marks the object after a consonant
듣다 is irregular: ㄷ → ㄹ before a vowel

form.q_en: Pick the particle that makes 'words' the object.
form.why: 말 ends in a consonant, so the object particle is 을. 를 follows a vowel, 이 marks a subject, and 에 means 'at/to'.

ko_meaning_en: Moving your body to stay healthy

tokens.note: 는 marks the topic after a vowel
을 marks the object after a consonant

form.q_en: Pick the particle that makes 'exercise' the object.
form.why: 운동 ends in a consonant (ㅇ), so it takes 을. 를 follows a vowel, 이 marks a subject, and 에 means 'at/to'.

ko_meaning_en: A story on screen that you watch at a cinema or on TV

example.en: I watched a movie on the weekend.

tokens.note: 를 marks the object after a vowel

form.q_en: Pick the correct past tense of 보다 (to watch).
form.why: 보다 has ㅗ, so it takes -았어요, and 보 + 았어요 shortens to 봤어요.

ko_meaning_en: Songs or sounds of instruments that you hear

tokens.note: 저 is the polite word for 'I'; 는 marks the topic
을 marks the object after a consonant

form.q_en: Pick the particle that goes with 좋아해요 (to like).
form.why: 좋아하다 takes an object, and 음악 ends in a consonant, so use 을. 를 follows a vowel; 에 and 이 do not fit.

ko_meaning: 다른 곳이나 나라에 가서 보고 즐기는 것
ko_meaning_en: Going to another place or country to see and enjoy it

example.en: I want to go on a trip with my family.

tokens.note: 을 marks the object after a consonant

form.q_en: Pick the particle: '여행 ___ 가다' means 'to go on a trip'.
form.why: Korean says 여행을 가다. 여행 ends in a consonant, so 을, not 를. 이 and 에서 do not fit.

ko_meaning_en: A picture taken with a camera

example.en: I took a photo with my friend.

tokens.note: 을 marks the object after a consonant

form.q_en: Pick the particle that makes 'photo' the object.
form.why: 사진 ends in a consonant, so the object particle is 을. 를 follows a vowel, 이 marks a subject, and 에 means 'at/to'.

ko_meaning_en: To spend time having fun

tokens.note: 에서 marks where an action happens

form.q_en: Yesterday the children played outside. Pick the past form.
form.why: 놀다 has ㅗ in its stem, so it takes -았어요: 놀았어요. 놀아요 is present tense.

ko_meaning_en: To go on foot, one step at a time

tokens.note: 가 marks the subject after a vowel
걷다 is irregular: ㄷ → ㄹ before a vowel

form.q_en: Pick the correct polite form of 걷다 (to walk).
form.why: 걷다 is irregular: ㄷ becomes ㄹ before a vowel, so 걷 + 어요 → 걸어요.

ko_meaning_en: To go very fast on foot

example.en: The dog runs in the park.

tokens.note: 가 marks the subject after a vowel
에서 marks where an action happens

form.q_en: Pick the correct polite form of 달리다 (to run).
form.why: When the stem ends in 리, 리 + 어요 combine into 려요: 달려요.

ko_meaning: 노래를 하다. 또는 이름을 말해서 오게 하다
ko_meaning_en: To sing a song; or to say a name to make someone come

example.en: My older sister sings a song.

tokens.note: 가 marks the subject after a vowel
를 marks the object after a vowel

form.q_en: Pick the correct polite form of 부르다 (to sing).
form.why: 부르다 is a 르 irregular verb: 르 drops and an extra ㄹ is added, so 부르 + 어요 → 불러요.

ko_meaning_en: To make a photo with a camera

example.en: I want to take a photo here.

tokens.note: 에서 marks where an action happens
을 marks the object after a consonant

form.q_en: Pick the form that goes before 싶어요 (want to).
form.why: To say 'want to', add -고 싶어요 to the verb stem: 찍 + 고 싶어요.

ko_meaning_en: To give something and receive money for it

example.en: They sell fruit at the market.

tokens.note: 에서 marks where an action happens
을 marks the object after a consonant

form.q_en: Pick the correct polite present form of 팔다.
form.why: 팔다 has ㅏ in the stem, so it takes -아요: 팔 + 아요 → 팔아요.

ko_meaning_en: The price is low

example.en: Fruit is cheap at the market.

tokens.note: 은 marks the topic after a consonant
이 marks the subject after a consonant

form.q_en: Pick the correct polite form of 싸다 (to be cheap).
form.why: When the stem ends in ㅏ, the 아 of -아요 drops: 싸 + 아요 → 싸요.

ko_meaning_en: The price is high

tokens.note: 는 marks the topic after a vowel

form.q_en: Pick the correct past tense of 비싸다.
form.why: Past tense: 비싸 + 았어요 shortens to 비쌌어요.

ko_meaning: 물건을 살 때 내는 돈, 값
ko_meaning_en: The money you pay when you buy something; the cost

example.en: How much is it? (What is the price?)

tokens.note: 이 marks the subject after a consonant

form.q_en: Pick the particle that makes 'price' the subject.
form.why: 가격 ends in a consonant, so the subject particle is 이 (가 follows a vowel). 을 and 에 do not fit.

ko_meaning: 고마울 때나 축하할 때 주는 물건
ko_meaning_en: Something you give to say thanks or to celebrate

example.en: My friend gave me a present on my birthday.

tokens.note: 가 marks the subject after a vowel
을 marks the object after a consonant

form.q_en: Pick the correct past tense of 주다 (to give).
form.why: 주다 has ㅜ, so it takes -었어요, and 주 + 었어요 shortens to 줬어요.

ko_meaning_en: Much more than usual

form.q_en: Pick the word that means 'very' before an adjective.
form.why: 아주 is an adverb, so it can go before the adjective 맛있어요. 큰, 커요 and 크다 are forms of the adjective 크다 and cannot do that.

ko_meaning_en: In a small amount or degree

tokens.note: 을 marks the object after a consonant

form.q_en: Pick the word that means 'a little' before a verb.
form.why: 조금 is an adverb that goes before the verb. 적은, 적어요 and 적다 are forms of the adjective 적다 and cannot describe 마셨어요.

ko_meaning_en: In a large number or amount

example.en: I slept a lot on the weekend.

form.q_en: Pick the adverb form of 많다 (to be many).
form.why: 많이 is the adverb ('a lot') that describes the verb 왔어요. 많은, 많아요 and 많다 are adjective forms.

ko_meaning_en: Two or more, at the same time and place

example.en: I eat lunch together with my friend.

tokens.note: 을 marks the object after a consonant

form.q_en: Pick the particle that goes with 같이 for 'together with a friend'.
form.why: 하고 (or 와/과) + 같이 means 'together with'. 를, 의 and 에서 do not fit here.

ko_meaning_en: One more time

form.q_en: Pick the polite request form of 오다 (to come).
form.why: After a vowel stem, add -세요 directly: 오 + 세요 → 오세요 (please come).

ko_meaning_en: In a short time

tokens.note: 이 marks the subject after a consonant

form.q_en: Pick the adverb that means 'quickly'.
form.why: 빨리 is the adverb that describes how time goes. 빠른, 빨라요 and 빠르다 are forms of the adjective 빠르다.

ko_meaning_en: Slowly, without hurrying

form.q_en: Pick the polite request form of 말하다 (to speak).
form.why: The stem 말하- ends in a vowel, so add -세요 directly: 말하세요.

ko_meaning_en: Doing the same thing many times

example.en: I often go to the library.

tokens.note: 저 is the polite word for 'I'
에 marks the place you go to

form.q_en: Pick the particle for the place you go to.
form.why: With 가다 (to go), the destination takes 에. 에서 is for where an action happens; 을 and 이 do not fit.

ko_meaning_en: At all times

tokens.note: 는 marks the topic after a vowel

form.q_en: Pick the correct polite form of 바쁘다 (to be busy).
form.why: 바쁘다 drops ㅡ, and the vowel before it is ㅏ, so it takes -아요: 바빠요.

ko_meaning_en: Before other people or things

tokens.note: 을 marks the object after a consonant

form.q_en: Pick the polite request form of 씻다 (to wash).
form.why: The stem 씻- ends in a consonant, so add -으세요: 씻으세요.

ko_meaning: 지금도 계속, 또는 지금까지 안 되어서
ko_meaning_en: Even now; or not happened up to now

example.en: I haven't done my homework yet.

tokens.note: 를 marks the object after a vowel

form.q_en: Pick the word that makes the verb negative ('not yet').
form.why: 안 goes right before the verb to make it negative. 아니요 and 네 are answers ('no', 'yes'), and 없어 means 'there isn't'.

ko_meaning_en: Sooner than you thought; already

form.q_en: Pick the right ending for 'it is night'.
form.why: 밤 ends in a consonant, so use 이에요. 예요 is used after a vowel.

ko_meaning_en: Before much time passes; soon

tokens.note: 가 marks the subject after a vowel

form.q_en: Pick the correct polite form of 오다 (to come).
form.why: 오다 has ㅗ, so it takes -아요, and 오 + 아요 shortens to 와요.

ko_meaning_en: Not now, but some time after

form.q_en: Pick the particle that makes 나중 mean 'later'.
form.why: 나중 is a time word and takes 에 to mean 'at a later time'. 이, 를 and 의 do not fit here.

ko_meaning_en: From a little while ago until now

example.en: The weather is cold these days.

tokens.note: 가 marks the subject after a vowel

form.q_en: Pick the correct polite form of 춥다 (to be cold).
form.why: 춥다 is ㅂ irregular: ㅂ becomes 우 before a vowel, so 춥 + 어요 → 추워요.

ko_meaning_en: Not hard to do

tokens.note: 은 marks the topic after a consonant

form.q_en: Pick the correct past tense of 쉽다 (to be easy).
form.why: 쉽다 is ㅂ irregular: ㅂ changes to 우, so 쉽 + 었어요 → 쉬웠어요.

ko_meaning_en: Hard to do

tokens.note: 가 marks the subject after a vowel

form.q_en: Pick the word that means 'not' before an adjective.
form.why: 안 + adjective means 'not': 안 어려워요 = it isn't difficult. 못 (cannot) is not used with adjectives, and 아니요/없어 do not fit.

ko_meaning_en: The distance is short

example.en: The school is close to my home.

tokens.note: 가 marks the subject after a vowel

form.q_en: Pick the particle that means 'from' here.
form.why: 에서 can mean 'from': 집에서 가까워요 = close from home. 을 and 의 do not fit, and 와 is only used after a vowel.

ko_meaning_en: The distance is long

tokens.note: 은 marks the topic after a consonant

form.q_en: Pick the correct polite present form of 멀다.
form.why: 멀다 has ㅓ in the stem, so it takes -어요: 멀 + 어요 → 멀어요.

ko_meaning_en: Long from bottom to top

tokens.note: 이 marks the subject after a consonant

form.q_en: Pick the particle that makes 'sky' the subject.
form.why: 하늘 ends in a consonant, so the subject particle is 이 (가 follows a vowel). 을 and 에 do not fit.

ko_meaning_en: Short from bottom to top

example.en: The chair is a little low.

tokens.note: 가 marks the subject after a vowel

form.q_en: Pick the correct polite present form of 낮다.
form.why: 낮다 has ㅏ in the stem, so it takes -아요: 낮 + 아요 → 낮아요.

ko_meaning_en: It weighs a lot and is hard to lift

tokens.note: 이 marks the subject after a consonant

form.q_en: Pick the correct past tense of 무겁다 (to be heavy).
form.why: 무겁다 is ㅂ irregular: ㅂ becomes 우, so 무겁 + 었어요 → 무거웠어요.

ko_meaning_en: It weighs little and is easy to lift

tokens.note: 은 marks the topic after a consonant

form.q_en: Pick the correct polite form of 가볍다 (to be light).
form.why: 가볍다 is ㅂ irregular: ㅂ becomes 우 before a vowel, so 가볍 + 어요 → 가벼워요.

ko_meaning_en: Moving a lot in a short time

tokens.note: 가 marks the subject after a vowel

form.q_en: Pick the correct polite form of 빠르다 (to be fast).
form.why: 빠르다 is a 르 irregular word: 르 drops and an extra ㄹ is added, so 빠르 + 아요 → 빨라요.

ko_meaning_en: Taking a long time to move

tokens.note: 가 marks the subject after a vowel

form.q_en: Pick the correct polite form of 느리다 (to be slow).
form.why: When the stem ends in 리, 리 + 어요 combine into 려요: 느려요.

ko_meaning: 어떤 것을 배워서 머리에 가지고 있다
ko_meaning_en: To have learned something and keep it in your head

tokens.note: 을 marks the object after a consonant

form.q_en: Pick the correct polite present form of 알다.
form.why: 알다 has ㅏ in the stem, so it takes -아요: 알 + 아요 → 알아요.

ko_meaning_en: To not know something

example.en: I don't know that person's name.

form.q_en: Yesterday I didn't know. Pick the past form of 모르다.
form.why: 모르다 is 르-irregular: 모르 + 았어요 → 몰랐어요. 몰라요 is present tense.

ko_meaning_en: To stay until a person or a time comes

example.en: I wait for my friend at the station.

tokens.note: 에서 marks where an action happens
를 marks the object after a vowel

form.q_en: Pick the particle for the person you wait for.
form.why: Korean says 'wait someone' with an object particle: 친구를 기다려요. 친구 ends in a vowel, so 를, not 을.

ko_meaning_en: To study something you do not know and come to know it

tokens.note: 에서 marks where an action happens
를 marks the object after a vowel

form.q_en: Pick the correct polite form of 배우다 (to learn).
form.why: 배우다 has ㅜ, so it takes -어요, and 우 + 어요 combine into 워요: 배워요.

ko_meaning_en: To do the first part of something

tokens.note: 이 marks the subject after a consonant
native numbers are used for hours

form.q_en: Pick the correct polite present form of 시작하다.
form.why: Verbs ending in 하다 change 하 + 여요 into 해요: 시작해요.
